translations.text: over all the world, among men, foreign speech in divided voices, varied and manifold, after Christ was in the world
The teacher [?] meant this about the foreign speech, when the Apostle said: "For if I do not know the meaning of the voice, I shall be a foreigner to the one I speak to
and the one who speaks to me is a foreigner to me." The same is also said of men and peoples who sometimes mean something about known matters
[and no one] knows what another foreign language's voice [means]; he knows nothing more unless the other makes the matter known to him in words. Almighty God, who created and
through God's word made what is made, and without him nothing that is made exists at all. He himself certainly knows men's
thoughts, pure and impure, in words and in works, [?] however much is laid up in the mind, and also the
divided voices in the foreign speech; as he certainly created it all, so likewise it is all plainly
open to him. And likewise Solomon, the wisest of kings, of whom it is said: "You alone, Lord, know the thoughts of all men."
And the same man, in his wisdom, said of God's power: "In every place the eyes of God watch and see
the good and the evil." And the noble teacher of the nations, Paul the Apostle, also said to the Hebrews: "The word of God is truly living
and more piercing than any two-edged weapon, and it reaches as far as the division of soul and spirit, and of a man's marrow and joints,
and it judges [the thoughts] of the heart and the loins." About this same distinction [?] it is said in the Psalms: "Praise the Lord, all nations, and likewise
let all peoples praise him." He himself foretold it, saying in prophecies: "Clap your hands, all nations, and shout to God with your voice." And as the same man also writes:
"Honour and a song of praise to you; let them sing to you, Most High." Through man, and his sorrowful [?] mercy,
he deigned to come down from heaven to earth, to endure humanity and to suffer death. In the same way he went down as a man to hell,
free among the dead; the all-ruling ones [?] could not hold him, and so he redeemed mankind. Victorious,
he returned in a man's body to the gates of his heavenly paradise, in heavenly power. The Holy Spirit was sent.
About this the teacher of the nations said: "You are all truly sons of God through firm faith in the saving
Christ. For as many of you as have been baptised in Christ's name have put on Christ." And as it is also
written: Christ is the head of all Christians, and all those chosen by God are the limbs of his head.
And the same Apostle also said this: "The love of God has been poured into the will of our minds through the Holy Spirit,
who was given to us." For without it you have nothing useful [?] that you can possess, for it is
joined with the Holy Spirit. "The love of God is patient; it is kind; it is not envious; it does not puff itself up
It has no vice; it is not greedy; it does not seek what is its own; it does not take offence; it thinks no evil; it does not rejoice over
injustice; it rejoices together with truth. Patient indeed is the love of God, because it bears its adversities
with an even mind. It is kind, because it gently repays good for evil. It is not envious,
because in this time it cares nothing at all for worldly possessions, nor does it know any envy
of earthly having. It does not puff itself up, because it anxiously desires the eternal benefit
of the inner reward, and therefore it does not raise itself up in these outward [?] powers. It does no wrong, because
it spreads itself out in the love of the one God and of the neighbour, and knows nothing that departs from what is right. It is not
ambitious, because, burning inwardly to strive for what belongs to it, it desires no [?] outward advancement in any way.
It does not seek what is its own, because all the transitory things it has here it cares for no more than what it
does not have, because it recognizes nothing as its own except that one thing which endures with it. It does not take offence,
because even when it is wounded by tribulations, it is not stirred to any vengeance, because
here, in the great toil [?], it awaits the greater reward afterwards. It thinks no evil, because
it keeps its mind fixed in purity. All hatred is turned away from it; it knows nothing that is unjust
in its nature. It does not rejoice in injustice, because in one love it sighs for all people, and it never rejoices in the
perdition of its adversaries. It rejoices equally with truth, because it loves others as it loves itself. And
whatever good it sees in another, it rejoices in it just as in its own benefits. And likewise
in the first commandment of God the Gospel means this, where the Lord answered the one who questioned him, saying: Love the Lord your
God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and strength. After this there is also another
commandment like it: Love your neighbour as yourself. By 'neighbours' Holy Scripture counts all
Christians and righteous people who are of one will to keep God's commandments. For one [?] God through [?]
the prophet [?], how the Lord spoke concerning them: I have no pleasure in you, says the Lord, and I will not accept a gift from your hand.
From where the sun rises in the east until it sets, great and glorious is [my name] among the peoples; in every place
[?] to my name a pure gift; my name [is great] among the peoples, he said. So we also read in the Acts [of the Apostles] that the Jewish
people, full of hatred, envied that the holy disciples of Christ were [?] the heathen peoples [?]
with words." Then at once Paul [and ?] said with one mind: "It was fitting that the word of God be spoken to you first, but because you [reject] it [?]
[?] you reject [it], and judge [yourselves] unworthy of the blessed [?], therefore we turn [?] to [?]. Indeed [?], the Lord;
And as it is written: "I have set you as a light to the peoples, that [?] unto the end of the earth." And when [they heard?] this, they were rejoicing at it,
and [glorified?] honourably [?]. And as many as were [ordained?] before to eternal life believed; as was written through
